title: Replay idempotent requests from the stored result, after re-authorising

facts.note: Bun conventions catalog; code may run on Node.
Key is read in routes, replay decided in the use case, key record persisted by the store adapter.
Task text names idempotent handling of a mutating operation.

A content observer must detect a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE handler or use case that reads a client-supplied idempotency key (header, body field or parameter). This alone is sufficient for activation; no defect finding is required.

fires: A POST handler accepts an Idempotency-Key header to debit an account balance or create an invoice.
A use case that reserves inventory stock or a booking takes a client-supplied request id meant to de-duplicate retries.
Existing replay code for a keyed mutating operation is changed, e.g. how the stored response is returned or how the key record is written.
doesNotFire: Operations idempotent by construction with no client key (e.g. PUT replacing a resource with the full given state).
Server-internal de-duplication of messages with no client-facing response (e.g. consumer offset tracking).

given: A mutating operation accepts a client-supplied idempotency key.
when: A request arrives whose key is already recorded in the same caller/resource scope.
then: After authorising the caller exactly as for a first request, return the stored original response verbatim if the payload fingerprint matches, else reject with a 4xx and change nothing — never re-execute side effects or recompute the result.
prefer: Persist per (scope, key) a fingerprint of the normalised payload plus the full original response (status, body), in the same transaction as the side effect.
Authenticate/authorise the caller before comparing the fingerprint or returning anything stored; then replay the stored response on match, or 409/422 on mismatch.
Claim the key inside the side effect's critical section (unique constraint, insert-if-absent, row lock) so concurrent duplicates cannot both run.
avoid: Treating a known key as a credential or skipping auth on replay.
Rebuilding the replay response from current prices, configuration or state.
Looking keys up by key string alone, globally (cross-tenant collisions).
Check-then-act: reading the key outside the transaction that performs the write.
why: Clients retry after timeouts; a replay must yield exactly the first outcome without doubling effects, and a guessed or leaked key must not grant access or another caller's response.
evidence: Test: replay with same key and payload causes no extra side effect and returns a body identical to the first response.
Test: same key with a different payload returns 4xx and leaves state unchanged.
Test: replay of a recorded key by a different caller is rejected exactly as that caller's first request would be (no stored response leaked).
Test: after a configuration/price change, replay returns the stored original result, not a recomputed one.
Test or review: two concurrent requests with the same key result in a single side effect.
verifier_detail: Key record is keyed by (caller or resource scope, key), never by key string alone.
Record holds a fingerprint (hash) of the normalised payload and the full response; it is written in the same atomic step as the side effect.
Authentication and authorisation succeed before the fingerprint comparison and before any stored response is returned; a stored response returned to an unauthorised caller is a finding.
Replay path does not re-execute the operation's side effects and does not call pricing/configuration/state readers to rebuild the response.
Mismatch path returns 4xx (409 Conflict or 422 Unprocessable) and does not execute the operation's side effects.
Concurrency: claim is enforced by unique constraint, conditional insert or lock within the same transaction; a separate read-then-write is a finding.
Optional diagnostic (not an activation condition, llm_judged): replay that recomputes, skips auth, is unscoped, or claims the key non-atomically.
audit: Written for PLT-85 as a new general convention from spec.md; no canonical source YAML.
